result.topic_en: Concluding step of an argument on primes in which, by comparing prime counts at shifted points q_1, q_r, Ramanujan derives that log p_r / log(1+1/r) equals log p_1 / log 2 + O(r).
result.transcription:
Add MS a 94 18 (53)

$\frac{\log p_1}{\log 2} - \frac{\log p_r}{\log(1+\frac{1}{r})} \geq O(r).$

Again supposing that $q_1 < p_1$, $q_r > p_r$, and
$\pi(q_1) = \pi(p_1) - n - 1$
$\pi(q_r) = \pi(p_r) + \left[\frac{n\log 2}{\log(1+\frac{1}{r})}\right]$
and proceeding as before we can show that
$\frac{\log p_1}{\log 2} - \frac{\log p_r}{\log(1+\frac{1}{r})} \leq O(r).$

It follows that
(1) $\frac{\log p_r}{\log(1+\frac{1}{r})} = \frac{\log p_1}{\log 2} + O(r).$

methods.what: Lower bound on the difference of normalized logarithms of primes
Choice of comparison points q_1, q_r defined via the prime-counting function to obtain the reverse inequality
Upper bound on the same difference
Combining both bounds into an asymptotic relation between log p_r and log p_1
